en.headline: Wong Tai Sin Temple lanterns stay lit through 4 October
en.dek: Sik Sik Yuen is keeping Mid-Autumn lanterns and late opening at Wong Tai Sin Temple through the National Day holiday week, with free admission.
body: Lanterns at Sik Sik Yuen Wong Tai Sin Temple will remain on display until 4 October, the temple operator said, covering an 18-day run that began on 17 September.

The displays, staged in the temple grounds and at Wong Tai Sin Temple Square, include traditional Mid-Autumn paper lanterns, temple-themed pieces and a lantern depicting a Hong Kong astronaut. Sik Sik Yuen said the programme also marks the 77th National Day and the organisation’s 105th anniversary.

Evening opening has been extended for the period: 9pm from Monday to Friday, 10pm on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, and 11pm on Mid-Autumn night on 25 September. Last admission is one hour before closing. Admission is free.

The operator has also scheduled lantern riddles, astronomy sessions, craft workshops on selected evenings and a nightly giveaway of a small lighted souvenir after 6pm while stocks last. Visitors were asked to follow on-site crowd controls if queues form.

zh.headline: 黃大仙祠中秋綵燈展至10月4日
zh.dek: 嗤色園黃大仙祠中秋綵燈及夜間延長開放安排持續至10月4日，國慶假期期間仍可免費入場。
body: 嗤色園表示，黃大仙祠中秋綵燈會由9月17日起一連18日舉行，展期至10月4日。
祠內及黃大仙廟宇廣場展出傳統中秋紮作花燈、黃大仙祠主題花燈，以及香港太空人造型花燈。嗤色園指活動同時紀念國慶77周年及該園105周年。
活動期間祠宇延長開放：星期一至五至晚上9時，星期六、日及公眾假期至晚上10時，中秋正日9月25日則至晚上11時，最後入場為關園前一小時。入場免費。
園方亦安排猜燈謎、觀星、指定晚上的手工工作坊，以及每晚6時後派發發光小禮物，送完即止。如現場人多，訪客須遵從人流管制指示。
